est: Est. 2026 · git for the agentic era
headline:
Git, split apart.
And put back together.
lede: Every file tears into lines, and every line keeps its own author and history. People and their agents work in the same code at the same moment, without stepping on each other, and it all closes back up as a real git commit.
breathe_home: Let your code live here, so your ideas aren't held back by the old ways of git.
breathe_product: Hosting the code is the easy part: it just makes the move off the old host painless. The scripts and feedback loops are the product.
helpers_title: Meet your helpers for the agentic era.
mervin: merges, and settles the clashes git gives up on
ester: sorts every red check: main's fault, flaky, or yours
dexter: finds where the tokens go and trims the context
helpers_learn: No model in any of them. Each answer you give can become a rule, so they learn your repo and need you less.
breathe_wasted: However smart, fast or cheap AI gets, it's wasted on deterministic chores.
stat_mervin: of the files git gave up on, Mervin settled with rules alone
stat_spend: of our own swarm's spend went to merge fights, test logs and oversized results: chores, not features
stat_cache: of 8.27 billion input tokens were cached re-reads of shared rules, over 25 days
stat_solved: clashes Mervin settled with no card
breathe_more_than_git: More than git: idle compute and cores, put to work, so your AI spend goes to adding value, not fixing itself.
breathe_scroll_on: the long version, if you've come this far
ai_label: why not let the AI do it?
ai_title: Spend the AI on the what, not the how
ai_blurb: We do use AI, and we want the most out of it. A merge, a red check, a bloated prompt: plain code already solved those, so paying a model to solve them again costs tokens, time and the features it could have built. It compounds like interest: every solved problem is one no agent pays for again, so each round goes further on less. Less intelligence fussing over the HOW, straight to the WHAT, because the WHY is already solved. By who? RustyBuns.
dots_label: wait, let me explain with dots
dots_title: Why thirty agents jam the old git way
dots_blurb: Each dot is an agent with a feature to ship. Picture a subway at rush hour: one jammed staircase, a ticket gate, a test exit. Then the three layers that fix it. Try the sliders. We got git problems with agent swarm has this and a real week of this repo replayed.
map_title: Everything it does, by what you're doing
map_blurb: Pick where you're standing. Every feature is on one of these tabs, with a picture of how it fits.
hand_title: Made for a human hand, as much as an agent's eye
hand_blurb: We aren't stuck in history. Every action is one call, and every door into it opens for a person or an agent: click it, type it, or hand it to a model. Same call, same result, same signed line.
host_title: Git it, get it, share it, agent it, socialize it
host_blurb: Human to human, human to agent, agent to agent, and everyone to the computer. Your agents don't get a sandbox off to the side: they work in the same repo as you, live, line by line, each line signed by whoever wrote it, and nothing ships until a person says so.
whatif_blurb: What if git was as public as you wanted to be, private as you wanted to be: here, there, everywhere. A line by line privacy model, making it easier to share more with human and agent alike.
desktop_blurb: You want to git commit, but is your git committed to you? Most hosts keep your git in their cloud and sync it down to you. The desktop app turns that around: your git lives on your machine, and syncs out to whatever clouds you like. If a cloud dies, you and your agents keep going.
strip_title: All of it, on one strip
strip_blurb: Drag it, or scroll sideways: it goes on as long as you do. Or read them as a list.
cmds_title: Everything is one command, for people and agents alike
cmds_blurb: Press <kbd>⌘K</kbd> anywhere. Each of these is a single call to the API underneath, so an agent can do anything you can.
shell_blurb: The same calls as a shell command, for you or for an agent that would rather run a command than speak MCP. One line installs it, on Bun or Node.
levels_blurb: Real repos, imported into Artifacts. Fork one into a git repo you own in one click (upstream stays as it was), browse it, or play it. {copy} copies a repo's GitHub link and drops it in the dig box below.
ai_how: Mervin merges, Ester sorts the red, Dexter trims the context. Rules and replay, no model, no tokens.
ai_why: Every agent starts from the same rules, so the model reads them from cache. Over 25 days of this repo's own agents, 97.8% of 8.27 billion input tokens were cached re-reads.
ai_what: Where the model's thinking goes. Those same 25 days shipped 1,490 changes to main.
take_control: What if your git got good?
codeSplitter: where the git got good.
AI has evolved the field, so why can't git evolve with it?
Innovate on git? Nah, I'm here for the games, but while I'm here I might as well git to it.
dig_why: In codeSplitter, “digging” is simply bringing code into the ecosystem: digging in for the long haul.
